Added a real `/admin` auth boundary using Next’s built-in `forbidden()` flow. The route now checks the session on each request and returns a proper 403 when `session.role !== 'admin'` in [app/admin/page.tsx](/vercel/sandbox/app/admin/page.tsx#L1). I also enabled `experimental.authInterrupts` in [next.config.ts](/vercel/sandbox/next.config.ts#L1) so the HTTP access boundary is active.

The 403 response renders a custom error page from [app/forbidden.tsx](/vercel/sandbox/app/forbidden.tsx#L1), with a styled forbidden screen instead of a generic fallback. Next also updated [tsconfig.json](/vercel/sandbox/tsconfig.json#L1) during the build to include its generated dev types.

Verified with `npm run build`. The final route manifest shows `/admin` as `ƒ (Dynamic)`, so the access check is evaluated server-side on demand rather than at build time.
